description: If your Cursor mac not working, follow this guide to resolve IDE errors, keyboard shortcut conflicts, and installation issues on your Apple computer.
intro: When you find your Cursor mac not working, the most effective solutions involve clearing corrupted cache files or resetting your local workspace state. You can usually restore full functionality by performing a clean restart of the application or by clearing specific configuration directories within your user library.
tldr: Quit Cursor using ⌘+Q to ensure all background processes stop.
Check the official status page to rule out service-wide outages.
Clear the globalStorage folder to reset persistent session freezes.
Use the built-in keyboard shortcut debugger to identify key conflicts.

blocks.text: Initial diagnostic steps for Cursor Mac not working

Before you dive into complex terminal commands, perform basic checks. First, verify that the issue is not a service outage. Visit the official status page to see if the Cursor servers are currently down. If the service is online, your issue is likely local. A full restart is the most common fix. Use ⌘+Q to quit the application entirely. Closing the window with the red button does not quit the app. It only hides it. A full quit forces the app to release locked files and clear transient memory. If you use a VPN or a corporate firewall, try disabling these services temporarily. Sometimes these tools block the API calls required for the AI features to function.

Many users report that their Cursor keyboard shortcuts not working due to conflicts with other macOS applications. Cursor is built on the VS Code architecture, so it respects the same keybinding system. You can debug this by opening the command palette with ⌘+⇧+P. Type Developer: Toggle Keyboard Shortcuts Troubleshooting. Once enabled, press the key combination that is failing. Cursor will log the command it detects. If nothing shows up, another app on your Mac is likely capturing that keystroke before it reaches the editor. Check your System Settings under Keyboard > Shortcuts to see if any system-level commands overlap with your IDE bindings.
Fixing installation errors and damaged app warnings

If macOS displays a warning that Cursor is damaged, it is often a false positive from the Gatekeeper security system. This happens when the application binary is flagged during an update. To fix this, move your current app to the Trash. Download a fresh installer from the official Cursor website. If the warning persists, you can manually clear the quarantine attribute. Open your Terminal.app and enter the following command: sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cursor.app. This command removes the security flag that prevents the app from launching. Follow this with sudo xattr -cr /Applications/Cursor.app to ensure the file structure is verified. You will need your Mac administrator password to run these commands.
Clearing cache and database files for performance

Persistent freezes or slow performance often stem from a bloated database file. Cursor stores its state in a local SQLite database. You can safely remove these files to reset the app state. Quit Cursor first. Open Finder and press ⌘+⇧+G to open the Go to Folder prompt. Paste the path ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/globalStorage/. Inside this folder, you will find files like state.vscdb. If this file is extremely large, it may be causing the editor to hang. Deleting this file forces Cursor to rebuild its internal state. Your project code and settings will remain untouched. Only the session-specific metadata is cleared. Restart the application after deleting the file to let it re-initialize.
Workspace trust and disk access permissions

Sometimes the AI agent cannot access files in your current workspace. This is often a permission issue. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access on your Mac. Ensure the toggle for Cursor is turned on. Without this, the editor cannot index your local files properly. If you are working in a sensitive directory, you may also need to manually trust the workspace. When you open a new folder, Cursor usually prompts you to trust the authors. If you dismissed this, you can manually add the folder to your trusted list via the settings menu. This ensures the AI has the necessary read and write permissions to perform code edits.

faq.question: Why does my Cursor app say it is damaged?
faq.answer: This is a macOS Gatekeeper security issue. You can resolve it by re-downloading the app or using the xattr terminal command to remove the quarantine flag from the application file.

faq.question: How do I fix keyboard shortcuts that are not working?
faq.answer: Use the command palette to run Developer: Toggle Keyboard Shortcuts Troubleshooting. This helps you identify if another app is intercepting your keys or if there is a conflict in your settings.

faq.question: Does clearing the globalStorage folder delete my code?
faq.answer: No. Removing the contents of the globalStorage folder only resets the editor's session state, such as open tabs and window positions. Your actual project files remain completely safe.

faq.question: What should I do if the AI chat stops responding?
faq.answer: First, check your internet connection and ensure your VPN is off. If that fails, sign out and back into your account in the Cursor settings to refresh your authentication token.
